question.problem:
Given the function $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{yz}$, compute ${∇}_{x,y}({∇}_{x,y}\,f).$
${∇}_{x,y}({∇}_{x,y}f)=\text{ }$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}}
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the variable subset gradient:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x,y}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{yz}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{yz})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{yz} \\ xz{e}^{yz}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the second derivatives with respect to $x$ and $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{yz})=0\,\, &  & \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{yz})=z{e}^{yz} \\  & \frac{∂}{∂x}(xz{e}^{yz})=z{e}^{yz}\,\, &  & \frac{∂}{∂y}(xz{e}^{yz})=x{z}^{2}{e}^{yz}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x,y}({∇}_{x,y}\,f) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & z{e}^{yz} \\ z{e}^{yz} & x{z}^{2}{e}^{yz}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
